questions.text: The Bauhaus Building in Dessau (1926) was designed by Walter Gropius. What features make its workshop wing a landmark of early Modernism?

options.text: Board-marked béton brut surfaces, deep cantilevers, and a pilotis-raised volume floating above the ground plane
A glass curtain-wall workshop wing, an asymmetric pinwheel plan, and flat roofs — the Bauhaus teaching itself
A glass-corner curtain wall eliminating the corner column, classified as a UNESCO World Heritage precursor
A cofferred steel roof resting on eight cruciform columns enclosing a single universal column-free space

rationale.summary: The Dessau Bauhaus Building has a glass curtain-wall workshop wing, asymmetric pinwheel plan, and flat roofs.
rationale.explanation: The article's table describes the Bauhaus Building, Dessau as 'glass curtain wall workshop wing, asymmetric pinwheel plan, flat roofs; the Bauhaus teaching itself.' This building physically embodied the school's principles and is the peak institutional product of the Dessau phase.
common_misconceptions: Option A describes Brutalist characteristics (béton brut, pilotis) — associated with Le Corbusier
Option C describes the Fagus Factory (Gropius and Meyer, 1911), a different earlier building in Alfeld

questions.explanation: Tests understanding of the Dessau Bauhaus Building's defining architectural features.

It introduced exposed color-coded mechanical systems as primary aesthetic elements on a factory exterior
It was the first building to use ETFE foil panels and parametric digital fabrication in a factory setting
It pioneered the glass-corner curtain wall, eliminating the corner column, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site

rationale.summary: The Fagus Factory pioneered the glass-corner curtain wall with no corner column and is a UNESCO Heritage site.

common_misconceptions: ETFE and parametric fabrication are 21st-century techniques — the Fagus Factory is from 1911
Color-coded mechanical systems are a High-Tech characteristic (Centre Pompidou, 1977), not Bauhaus

questions.explanation: Tests knowledge of the Fagus Factory's structural innovation and its UNESCO status.

questions.text: The Bauhaus Weimar phase (1919–1925) is characterized by which pedagogical approach and which faculty members?

Pure architecture focus following the departure of fine artists; led by Hannes Meyer from 1928 to 1930, which was after the Weimar phase

Option A describes the Dessau phase; Option C and D also describe other phases.
common_misconceptions: Albers, Moholy-Nagy, and Breuer are associated with the Dessau phase (1925–1932), not Weimar
Hannes Meyer directed only during the late Dessau phase (1928–1930), not the Weimar phase

questions.text: The 1932 MoMA exhibition that defined the 'International Style' was organized by which two figures, and what was the exhibition's full title?

options.text: Henry-Russell Hitchcock and Philip Johnson; 'Modern Architecture: International Exhibition'
Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret; 'Five Points: A New Architecture for the 20th Century'
Walter Gropius and Ludwig Mies van der Rohe; 'Modern Architecture: The Bauhaus Contribution'
Alison and Peter Smithson; 'New Brutalism: Architecture Since 1945'

rationale.summary: Henry-Russell Hitchcock and Philip Johnson organized 'Modern Architecture: International Exhibition' at MoMA in 1932.
rationale.explanation: The article states: 'The critic Henry-Russell Hitchcock and the architect/curator Philip Johnson organized the 1932 MoMA exhibition Modern Architecture: International Exhibition and co-authored The International Style: Architecture Since 1922, which gave the movement its name.'
common_misconceptions: Gropius and Mies were practitioners displayed IN the exhibition, not the curators who organized it
The Smithsons are associated with Brutalism (New Brutalism), not the International Style

questions.explanation: Tests recall of the curators and title of the 1932 MoMA exhibition that named the International Style.

questions.text: that 'Bauhaus' and 'International Style' are often treated as synonyms. What correctly distinguishes them?

options.text: The Bauhaus is a school (institution and pedagogy); the International Style is a critical label applied by Hitchcock and Johnson to multiple architects across many countries
The Bauhaus produced only furniture and graphics; the International Style refers exclusively to large-scale architectural buildings, focusing on skyscrapers and urban developments
They are functionally synonymous — all International Style buildings emerged from Bauhaus graduates working internationally, spreading the design principles globally
The Bauhaus lasted from 1919 to 1933; the International Style is the German term for the same movement after 1933, reflecting its evolution and adaptation

rationale.summary: Bauhaus = school (institution + pedagogy); International Style = a critical label applied retrospectively to many architects.
rationale.explanation: The article's Trap 2 states: 'The Bauhaus is a school (Weimar → Dessau → Berlin, 1919–1933). The International Style is a critical label applied by Hitchcock and Johnson in 1932 to buildings by multiple architects across multiple countries. Not all International Style buildings are Bauhaus; not all Bauhaus work is International Style (early Weimar-phase work was Expressionist).'
common_misconceptions: The early Weimar Bauhaus was Expressionist/craft-focused — it did not produce International Style architecture
International Style included non-Bauhaus architects like Le Corbusier, J.J.P. Oud, and others

questions.explanation: Tests the documented LEA Trap 2: treating Bauhaus and International Style as synonymous terms.

questions.text: that the Bauhaus was not exclusively about architecture. Which Bauhaus-produced work proves this interdisciplinary scope?

options.text: Marcel Breuer's Wassily Chair (1925), Herbert Bayer's Universal typeface, and Marianne Brandt's metalwork
The Fagus Factory (1911) and the Dessau Bauhaus Building (1926) — both by Gropius and representing pure architectural output
Mies's Barcelona Pavilion (1929) and the Tugendhat House (1930) — both designed during his directorship
The Schröder House (Rietveld, 1924) and the Villa Savoye (Le Corbusier, 1931) as International Style examples

rationale.summary: Breuer's Wassily Chair, Bayer's Universal typeface, and Brandt's metalwork prove the Bauhaus's interdisciplinary scope.
rationale.explanation: The article's Trap 3 states: 'The Bauhaus integrated all design disciplines — furniture (Breuer's Wassily Chair, 1925), typography (Herbert Bayer's Universal typeface), textiles (Anni Albers), metalwork (Marianne Brandt), and theater (Oskar Schlemmer). ALE questions may test this interdisciplinary scope.'
common_misconceptions: The Barcelona Pavilion (Mies, 1929) was designed after Mies left the Bauhaus — it is not a school product
Rietveld and Le Corbusier were not Bauhaus — they are De Stijl and International Style independently

questions.explanation: Tests the documented LEA Trap 3: thinking the Bauhaus was only about architecture.

questions.text: The phrase 'Form follows function' was coined by which architect, in which publication, and in what year?

options.text: Walter Gropius, in the Bauhaus Manifesto of 1919, as the foundational principle of the new school's pedagogy
Le Corbusier, in Vers une Architecture (1923), as part of his argument for the machine for living
Louis Henry Sullivan, in 'The Tall Office Building Artistically Considered,' published in 1896
Mies van der Rohe, in his 1938 inaugural address as Director of the Illinois Institute of Technology

rationale.summary: Louis Henry Sullivan coined 'Form follows function' in his 1896 essay on the tall office building.
rationale.explanation: The article states: 'Coined by American architect Louis Henry Sullivan in his 1896 essay The Tall Office Building Artistically Considered.' The article's Trap 1 explicitly warns this is frequently misattributed to Gropius, Le Corbusier, or Mies. Sullivan was a pre-Modernist Chicago School architect and mentor to Frank Lloyd Wright.
common_misconceptions: This is the documented ALE Trap 1 — the phrase is consistently misattributed to Bauhaus or Modernist architects
Sullivan preceded the Bauhaus by 23 years and the International Style by 36 years

questions.explanation: Tests the most commonly misattributed phrase in architectural history — LEA Trap 1 in the article.

questions.text: Louis Sullivan's Wainwright Building (1891) in St. Louis and Carson, Pirie, Scott Building (1899) in Chicago are?. Why are they included in a discussion of the Bauhaus and International Style?

options.text: Both buildings were featured in the 1932 MoMA International Style exhibition as American precursors to the European movement
Sullivan designed both buildings as Bauhaus equivalents in the American context, creating a parallel school in Chicago
Both buildings use flat roofs, no applied ornament, and glass curtain walls, qualifying them as early International Style examples
Sullivan coined 'Form follows function,' which the Bauhaus and International Style adopted; these buildings are where the principle originated

rationale.summary: Sullivan's buildings are included because he coined 'Form follows function,' which the Bauhaus and International Style adopted as a governing principle.
rationale.explanation: The article explains that Sullivan coined 'Form follows function' in 1896, and the Bauhaus and International Style adopted it. The Wainwright Building is described as 'Sullivan's tall office building with a tripartite composition (base-shaft-capital); where Form Follows Function was born.' Sullivan himself still used ornament but provided the principle.
common_misconceptions: Sullivan did NOT participate in the 1932 MoMA exhibition — he died in 1924
Option D is wrong — the Carson, Pirie, Scott Building has cast-iron ornament at street level, disqualifying it as pure International Style

questions.explanation: Tests critical evaluation of why Sullivan's pre-Modernist buildings are contextually relevant to the Bauhaus and International Style article.

questions.text: The Bauhaus school operated in three cities before its closure in 1933. What is the correct chronological sequence?

options.text: Berlin (1919) → Dessau (1925) → Weimar (1932), moving westward as Nazi political pressure increased
Dessau (1919) → Weimar (1925) → Berlin (1932), following the careers of its successive directors

rationale.explanation: The article states: 'The Bauhaus was founded in Weimar (1919), relocated to Dessau (1925) where Gropius built the iconic school building, and finally moved to Berlin (1932) under Mies van der Rohe's directorship before being forced to close by the Nazi regime in 1933.' The mnemonic is 'Gropius W-D-M-B: Weimar, Dessau, Mies, Berlin.'
common_misconceptions: The school moved east (Weimar → Dessau → Berlin), not west

questions.text: Hitchcock and Johnson defined three formal principles of the International Style in 1932. Which statement correctly identifies all three?

options.text: Pilotis, free plan, and ribbon windows — the liberation of building elements from load-bearing masonry constraints
Volume over mass, regularity over symmetry, and the absence of applied ornament
Truth to materials, structural expression, and monumental scale as civic expression
Complexity, contradiction, and historical layering as alternatives to Modernist purity

rationale.summary: The three International Style principles are: volume over mass, regularity over symmetry, no applied ornament.
rationale.explanation: The article's table lists Hitchcock and Johnson's three principles: '1. Volume over Mass — buildings conceived as thin-surfaced volumes enclosing space, not heavy masonry masses. 2. Regularity over Symmetry — structural grids and modular repetition replace Classical bilateral symmetry. 3. No Applied Ornament — beauty from proportion, material, and detail.' The mnemonic is VRO (Volume, Regularity, no Ornament).
common_misconceptions: Option A is Le Corbusier's Five Points — a different system entirely
Option C describes Brutalist principles; Option D describes Post-Modernism (Venturi)

questions.explanation: Tests recall of Hitchcock and Johnson's three International Style principles — the VRO framework.
